chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-' from Al-'Ala' ibn Kamil, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and fearfully, and without being loud in speech during the evening.'

'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no Associate for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He causes to live and causes to die, and He causes to die and causes to live, and He is Able upon everything.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'In His Hand is the goodness'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'In His Hand is the goodness, but say just as I am saying it to you, ten times, and, 'I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing', when the sun emerges and when it sets, ten times'.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He causes to live and causes to die

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method and content for evening and morning dhikr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on private, humble dhikr as a spiritual discipline, specifically linking the recitation of divine attributes to the transitional times of sunset and sunrise. It underscores the concept of Allah’s absolute sovereignty over life and death, while prescribing specific protective supplications to guard against the evils associated with the changing of day and night.

en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from al-‘Ala’ ibn Kamil who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying in the evening, ‘Remember (speak of) your Lord deep within yourselves, humbly and privately, instead of shouting out loud, (in prayer) in the mornings and evenings and do not be of the heedless ones,’ [7:205]

and ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah alone. Who has no partner. To Him belongs the kingdom and all praise. He gives life, causes death, causes death and gives life and He has power over all things.’

I (the narrator) said, ‘In His hand is all good.’ The Imam said, ‘All good is in His hand, however, say as 1 say to you ten times and say, ‘I seek protection with Allah, all Hearing and Omniscient,’ at sunrise and at sunset, ten times.”
